title: Greedy Best-First in Lisbon: Rush vs Reality ⚡
description: Greedy Best-First uses a heuristic to sprint toward the goal, often finding a fast path—but not always the safest one. Watch how it behaves on a real city grid and compare it conceptually to A* when the heuristic misleads.
ig_caption:
Greedy Best-First Search vs A*: Pathfinding Comparison — Why Greedy Best-First Search rushes toward destinations and when it fails ⚡

In this Lisbon (Alfama) map run, we’re doing graph search with a priority queue—but the priority is ONLY the heuristic h(n) (distance-to-goal estimate). ✅

What you’ll see in the visualization:
1) It expands the “most promising” node first (lowest h), so it looks fast.
2) It does NOT account for the path cost so far (no g(n) term like A*).
3) When obstacles or winding streets make the straight-line guess wrong, Greedy can detour, backtrack, or settle for a longer route.

Greedy vs A* (quick mental model):
- Greedy Best-First: picks by h(n) only → speed-first, quality-not-guaranteed.
- A*: balances f(n)=g(n)+h(n) → usually more reliable for optimal paths.

Takeaway: heuristic pathfinding can feel intelligent, but “closest-looking” isn’t always “best.”

Debate question: If your heuristic is slightly wrong, would you prefer Greedy for speed or A* for consistency? 👇
